settings.name_in_paper: Linearly parameterized bandit with a strongly convex arm set (SBAR(J) condition)
unmapped: Compact arm set satisfying the smooth best arm response condition SBAR(J), which is equivalent to strong convexity of the arm set
Arm norms bounded by u_bar; the learner knows r linearly independent arms b_k with lambda_min(sum b_k b_k') >= lambda_0
Unknown parameter Z is random, with a prior (Bayes risk)
settings.definition_quote: a set of arms~$\CAL U_r$ satisfies the {\em smooth best arm response with parameter $J$} (SBAR($J$), for short) condition if for any nonzero vector $\BF z$, there is a unique best arm $\BF u^*(\BF z)$ ... and $\norm{ \BF u^*(\BF z) - \BF u^*(\BF y) } \leq J \norm{ \BF z - \BF y}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Linearly parameterized bandit with a general compact set of arms
unmapped: Arbitrary compact (not necessarily convex) arm set with arm norms bounded by u_bar; contains r linearly independent arms with lambda_min >= lambda_0
Unknown parameter Z is random, with a prior (Bayes risk)
settings.definition_quote: We have a compact set $\CAL U_r \subset \Real^r$ that corresponds to the set of arms, where $r \geq 2$. The reward $X_t^{\BF u}$ of playing arm $\BF u$ in period $t$ is given by $X_t^{\BF u} = \BF u^\prime \BF Z + W_t^{\BF u}$

settings.name_in_paper: Linearly parameterized bandit with finitely many arms
unmapped: Unknown parameter Z is random, with a prior (Bayes risk)
Arm norms bounded by u_bar; contains r linearly independent arms with lambda_min >= lambda_0
settings.definition_quote: When the number of arms is finite, it turns out that we can obtain bounds on regret and risk that scale more gracefully over time, growing as $\log T$ and $\log^2 T$, respectively.

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem where the set of arms is the unit sphere in $\Real^r$, and $W^{\BF u}_t$ has a standard normal distribution ... If $\BF Z$ has a multivariate normal distribution with mean $\BF 0$ and covariance matrix $\BF I_r / r$, then for all policies $\psi$ and every $T \geq r^2$, ${\rm Risk}(T,\psi) \geq 0.006 \,r\, \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Paper's dimension r is mapped to d. Bayes risk under the Gaussian prior.

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: Consequently, for any policy $\psi$ and $T \geq r^2$, there exists $\BF z \in \Real^r$ such that ${\rm Regret}(\BF z, T, \psi) \geq 0.006 \, r \, \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Follows from the Bayes risk bound. Regret is defined as the expected gap given Z=z, i.e. pseudo-regret.

symbols.z_norm: Euclidean norm of the true parameter z
symbols.a_1: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0, J

extra_assumptions: Assumption 1 (sub-Gaussian noise with parameter sigma_0; arm norms <= u_bar; r linearly independent arms with lambda_min >= lambda_0)

source.label: theorem:greedy-regret
source.quote: Suppose that Assumption 1 holds and that the sets $\CAL U_r$ satisfy the SBAR($J$) condition. Then, there exists a positive constant $a_1$ that depends only on $\sigma_0$, $\bar{u}$, $\lambda_0$, and $J$, such that for any $\BF z \in \Real^r \setminus \{\BF 0\}$ and $T \geq r$, ${\rm Regret}(\BF z, T, \textsc{PEGE}) \leq a_1 ( \norm{\BF z} + \frac{1}{\norm{\BF z}} ) r \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: PEGE's cycle structure does not depend on T, so the bound is anytime. Recorded as O because the constant a_1 is unspecified.

symbols.a_2: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0, J, M

extra_assumptions: E[||Z||] <= M and E[1/||Z||] <= M for all r

source.label: theorem:greedy-regret
source.quote: Suppose in addition, that there exists a constant $M > 0$ such that for every $r\geq 2$ we have $\E[\norm{\BF Z}] \leq M$ and $\E[1/\norm{\BF Z}] \leq M$. Then, there exists a positive constant $a_2$ ... such that for any $T \geq r$, ${\rm Risk}(T, \textsc{PEGE}) \leq a_2 \, r \, \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Bayes risk under the prior on Z.

symbols.z_norm: Euclidean norm of the true parameter z

source.label: co:matching-upper-bounds
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem where the set of arms is the unit sphere in $\Real^r$, and where $W^{\BF u}_t$ has a standard normal distribution ... Then, there exists an absolute constant $a_3$ such that for any $\BF z \in \Real^r \setminus \{\BF 0\}$ and $T \geq r$, ${\rm Regret}(\BF z, T, \textsc{PEGE}) \leq a_3 ( \norm{\BF z} + \frac{1}{\norm{\BF z}} ) r \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Specialisation of Theorem 3.1 to the unit sphere.

source.label: co:matching-upper-bounds
source.quote: Moreover, if $\BF Z$ has a multivariate normal distribution with mean $\BF 0$ and covariance matrix $\BF I_r / r$, then for all $T \geq r$, ${\rm Risk}(T, \textsc{PEGE}) \leq a_3 \, r \sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Matches the lower bound of Theorem 2.1.

bound.expression_latex: a_4 r \norm{\BF z} + a_5 \, r \, \sqrt{T} \, \log^{3/2} T

symbols.z_norm: Euclidean norm of the true parameter z
symbols.a_4: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0
symbols.a_5: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0

source.label: theorem:UE-regret-analysis
source.quote: Under Assumption 1, there exist positive constants $a_4$ and $a_5$ that depend only on the parameters $\sigma_0$, $\bar{u}$, and $\lambda_0$, such that for all $T \geq r+1$ and $\BF z \in \Real^r$, ${\rm Regret}(\BF z, T, \textsc{UE}) \leq a_4 r \norm{\BF z} + a_5 \, r \, \sqrt{T} \, \log^{3/2} T$

results.notes: UE is anytime, as the paper states explicitly. The ||z|| term is lower order.

bound.expression_latex: a_4 r \, \E[\norm{\BF Z}] + a_5 \, r \, \sqrt{T} \, \log^{3/2} T

symbols.a_4: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0
symbols.a_5: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0

source.label: theorem:UE-regret-analysis
source.quote: ${\rm Risk}(T, \textsc{UE}) \leq a_4 r \, \E[\norm{\BF Z}] + a_5 \, r \, \sqrt{T} \, \log^{3/2} T$.

bound.expression_latex: a_6 \abs{\CAL U_r} \norm{\BF z} + a_7 \abs{\CAL U_r} \sum_{\BF u \in \CAL U_r} \min\left\{ \frac{\log T}{\Delta^{\BF u}(\BF z)}, T \Delta^{\BF u}(\BF z) \right\}

symbols.z_norm: Euclidean norm of the true parameter z
symbols.a_6: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0
symbols.a_7: constant depending only on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0

source.label: thm:regret-and-risk-small-arms
source.quote: Under Assumption 1, there exist positive constants $a_6$ and $a_7$ that depend only on the parameters $\sigma_0$, $\bar{u}$, and $\lambda_0$ such that for all $T \geq r+1$ and $\BF z \in \Real^r$, ${\rm Regret}(\BF z, T, \textsc{UE}) \leq a_6 \abs{\CAL U_r} \norm{\BF z} + a_7 \abs{\CAL U_r} \sum_{\BF u \in \CAL U_r} \min \{ \frac{\log T}{\Delta^{\BF u}(\BF z)}, T \Delta^{\BF u}(\BF z) \}$.

results.notes: K stands for |U_r|. The sum runs over all arms, and the min handles Delta = 0 (that term is 0).

bound.expression_latex: a_8 \abs{\CAL U_r} \E[\norm{\BF Z}] + a_9 \abs{\CAL U_r}^2 \log^2 T

symbols.a_8: constant depending on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0, M_0
symbols.a_9: constant depending on sigma_0, u_bar, lambda_0, M_0

extra_assumptions: for each arm, Delta^u(Z) has a point mass at 0 plus a density bounded by M_0 on R_+

source.label: thm:regret-and-risk-small-arms
source.quote: Moreover, suppose that there exists a positive constant $M_0$ such that, for all arms $\BF u$, the distribution of the random variable $\Delta^{\BF u}(\BF Z)$ is described by a point mass at $0$, and a density function that is bounded above by $M_0$ on $\Real_+$. Then ... ${\rm Risk}(T, \textsc{UE}) \leq a_8 \abs{\CAL U_r} \E[\norm{\BF Z}] + a_9 \abs{\CAL U_r}^2 \log^2 T$.
